title: Kuhl et al.'s existence conjecture for two-repetition gerechte designs with five subsquares
statement:
Let $h_1,\dots,h_5$ be positive integers, let $n=h_1+\cdots+h_5$, and let $[5]=\{1,2,3,4,5\}$. A $\operatorname{2-RP}(h_1\dots h_5)$ is a two-repetition gerechte design whose five subsquares have side lengths $h_1,\dots,h_5$. **Kuhl et al.'s existence conjecture.** A $\operatorname{2-RP}(h_1\dots h_5)$ exists if and only if

$$
n^2 - \sum_{i=1}^5h_i^2\geq 3\left( \sum_{i\in D}h_i\right)\left(\sum_{j\in\overline{D}}h_j\right)
$$

for all subsets $D$ of $[5]$ where $|D| = 3$. This gives necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of such designs with five subsquares; the source attributes the conjecture to Kuhl et al., and no resolution is supplied here.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.00967

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).
source_name: Tara Kemp, “Realizations with five subsquares”, arXiv:2406.00967 (2024).
